controls.title: Controlled entry points
controls.objective: Every exterior door and every door into a restricted area is controlled by an access control device or by staff.

evidence.description: Photo of each uncontrolled or propped door
Try every exterior door from outside

questions.text: Is every exterior door controlled by a card reader, keypad, lock, or a staffed post, with none found propped or unlocked without staff present?
questions.guidance: Try each door from outside. Partial: one door found unlocked with a documented reason. Photograph propped doors and the object used.

questions.text: Number of exterior or restricted-area doors found unlocked and unattended during the walk-through
questions.guidance: Count only doors that should be secured at the time of the walk. 0 is the expected result.

controls.title: Credential lifecycle
controls.objective: Access credentials are issued on documented authorization, reviewed periodically, and revoked promptly at separation.

evidence.description: Sample of separation records and access control system deactivation logs

questions.text: Longest time from separation to credential deactivation across the last 5 separations sampled
questions.guidance: Compare HR separation time with the access system audit log. Many organizations target same day (24 hours or less); record the measured maximum.

questions.text: Was a review of all active credentials against current staff lists completed in the last 6 months, with a dated record?
questions.guidance: Partial: review done but more than 6 and less than 12 months ago, or done without a record.

questions.text: Number of active credentials that do not match a current employee, contractor, or approved visitor
questions.guidance: Reconcile an export of active cards against the HR or contractor roster.

controls.title: Visitor management
controls.objective: Visitors are identified, recorded, visibly badged, and escorted in restricted areas, and badges are recovered.

evidence.description: Sign in as a visitor and observe the process
Visitor log for the last 30 days

questions.text: Are visitors required to show identification, sign in, and wear a badge visibly different from staff badges?
questions.guidance: Test by arriving as a visitor. Partial: sign-in without identification check, or badges indistinct from staff badges.

questions.text: Are visitors escorted at all times inside restricted areas, per written procedure and as observed?
questions.guidance: Observe at least one visitor movement if possible. Partial: procedure exists but escort not observed in practice.

questions.text: Are unreturned visitor badges reconciled at least daily, with temporary badges invalidated at sign-out?
questions.guidance: Check the visitor log against returned badges for one recent day.

controls.title: Door forced and held-open alarms
controls.objective: Controlled doors report forced-open and held-open conditions to a staffed monitoring point.

evidence.description: Hold a controlled door open and observe the alarm

questions.text: When a controlled door is forced or held open, does an alarm annunciate at a monitoring point staffed at that time?
questions.guidance: Test at least one exterior door with the operator's permission. Partial: alarm generated but only logged, not annunciated to a person.

questions.text: Measured time from holding a controlled door open until the held-open alarm is raised
questions.guidance: Use a stopwatch. Many sites set 30 to 60 seconds; record the measured value.

controls.title: Restricted area segregation
controls.objective: Server rooms, network closets, cash rooms, and other restricted rooms have separate access rights limited to named people.

evidence.description: Access group membership for each restricted room
Photo of restricted room doors and their locking hardware

questions.text: Is each server room and network closet locked and on an access group or key list limited to named people?
questions.guidance: Partial: room locked but access group includes broad groups such as 'all staff' or facilities contractors without need.

questions.text: Number of people with access to the main server or equipment room
questions.guidance: Count from the access control system or key register. Compare with the list of people whose duties require entry.

controls.title: Anti-tailgating at main entry
controls.objective: Main controlled entries prevent or detect more than one person entering on one authorization.

evidence.description: 15-minute observation at the main entry at peak time

questions.text: At the main controlled entry, is there a measure against tailgating (turnstile, mantrap, staffed post, or anti-passback with tailgate detection)?
questions.guidance: Partial: signage or policy only, with no physical or technical measure.

questions.text: Number of tailgating entries observed during a 15-minute observation at the main entry at peak arrival time
questions.guidance: Count people who entered without presenting a credential. Record the time window used.

controls.title: Loading dock and receiving control
controls.objective: Loading docks are secured when not in active use and receiving is separated from interior areas by a controlled door.

evidence.description: Photo of the dock door and the interior door from receiving

questions.text: Are dock doors closed and secured when no delivery is in progress?
questions.guidance: Observe for the period on site. Partial: closed but not locked.

questions.text: Is the receiving area separated from the rest of the building by a door that is locked or controlled?
questions.guidance: Photograph the separating door and its hardware.
